context: I-131 released from reactor exists as: (1) molecular iodine I2; (2) hydrogen iodide HI; (3) organic iodides (methyl iodide CH3I; ethyl iodide C2H5I; methylene iodide CH2I2); (4) particle-associated iodine (adsorbed on aerosols)
chernobyl_relevance: Chemical speciation determines: atmospheric residence time; dry deposition velocity; respiratory absorption efficiency; and therefore actual thyroid dose received
notes: Each form has very different environmental fate; the relative proportions change over time as I2 converts to organic forms via reaction with atmospheric hydrocarbons and OH•; underestimating organic iodide fraction → overestimating thyroid dose in far-field
source: Whitton 1993; NCRP Report 161 2009; Garland 1983 Atmos Environ; Chamberlain 1984

chernobyl_relevance: I2 (elemental/molecular iodine): 30-50% of total airborne I-131 immediately after Chernobyl release; most reactive form; highest deposition velocity and thyroid uptake; rapidly removed from air by: surface adsorption; reaction with NH3, NaHSO3; reaction with atmospheric dust particles
notes: I2 dominates initial near-field thyroid dose because: (1) high deposition velocity on grass/vegetation (Vd = 10-50 mm/s); (2) transferred efficiently to cow milk (Fm=0.004 d/L for I2); (3) high respiratory tract absorption ~0.9-1.0; near-field I-131 was primarily I2
source: Garland 1983; NRPB 1993; Chamberlain 1984 Atmos Environ; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv

chernobyl_relevance: Organic iodides (predominantly CH3I = methyl iodide): initially ~20-30% of I-131; fraction INCREASES with distance/time as I2 photolytically dissociates and reacts with atmospheric CH4/organic compounds; at 1000+ km: organic iodide may represent 50-70% of remaining I-131
notes: Increasing organic iodide fraction with distance means: far-field populations received proportionally LOWER thyroid doses per unit of airborne I-131 than near-field populations; near-field Swedish/Finnish populations received a mix with more I2 = higher dose per Bq/m³
source: Whitton 1993 NRPB R-254; IAEA 2006; thyroid dose modeling literature

chernobyl_relevance: Deposition velocity Vd(I2) = 10-50 mm/s on grass and vegetation (very fast); measured Vd for I2 onto short grass: ~15-20 mm/s; compared to Cs-137 aerosol Vd: ~0.5-2 mm/s (25-40x slower); explains why near-field vegetation I-131 contamination was much higher relative to Cs-137 than far-field contamination
notes: High Vd means I2 is rapidly removed from air to surfaces; short atmospheric residence time of hours-to-days for I2 means most I2 deposits near source; this is why Swedish levels of I-131 relative to Cs-137 were lower than near-Chernobyl levels

chernobyl_relevance: Deposition velocity Vd(CH3I) = 0.01-0.1 mm/s; 100-1000x lower than I2; consequently: (1) atmospheric residence time weeks; (2) travels much longer distances before depositing; (3) lower grassland/milk I-131 per unit airborne Bq; (4) lower thyroid dose per unit of airborne Bq
notes: For thyroid dose calculation: must know fraction of I-131 as I2 vs CH3I; error in this partition = factor 10-100 error in thyroid dose from inhalation; UNSCEAR 2008 uses typical environmental partition assumptions based on Chernobyl measurements
source: Garland 1983; Chamberlain 1984; UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D dosimetry

chernobyl_relevance: Particle-associated I-131 (adsorbed onto aerosol particles): ~15-30% of total release; deposition velocity similar to aerosol particles (Vd ~1-5 mm/s); thyroid absorption from inhalation ~0.4-0.6 (lower than I2 because particle filtration in upper respiratory tract)
notes: Particle-associated I-131 deposits with Cs-137 aerosols; provides similar spatial distribution; intermediate thyroid dose per unit airborne activity; particle sizes 0.5-3 µm (respirable range; submicron aerosols most efficient lung deposition)

chernobyl_relevance: Fm for I-131 transfer cow grass→milk = 0.004 d/L (Bq/L milk per Bq/day ingested by cow); derived from: cow consumes contaminated grass; I-131 absorbed in rumen; transferred to blood; secreted into milk; 8-12 hour delay from ingestion to milk peak
notes: This Fm value is critical for thyroid dose via milk pathway: milk contamination = air concentration × deposition velocity × grazing time × transfer factor; milk ban effectiveness depends on how quickly authorities acted post-deposition; Chernobyl: milk ban came too late in many areas (days after contamination)

chernobyl_relevance: Fm for I-131 in sheep milk = 0.29 d/L; 70x HIGHER than cow milk (0.004 d/L); because sheep are smaller, more metabolically active per unit body mass; sheep milk consumed directly by humans in Southern Europe (Greece Bulgaria Romania); partially explains why thyroid doses in southern European populations were higher per unit soil deposition than northern European
notes: soil_plant_transfer_factors_REAL.csv already notes this factor; Greek and Bulgarian children who consumed sheep cheese/yogurt may have received higher thyroid doses than estimated from deposition alone

chernobyl_relevance: Fraction of inhaled I-131 absorbed into blood by chemical form: I2 = 0.9-1.0 (nearly complete absorption via upper respiratory tract mucosa); CH3I = 0.2 (poorly absorbed); particle-associated = 0.4-0.6 (size-dependent alveolar deposition then clearance to gut); ICRP 30 used f1=1.0 for dietary I-131
notes: This determines inhalation dose: at same airborne Bq/m³, CH3I causes 5x less thyroid dose than I2; inaccurate chemical speciation → inaccurate dose reconstruction; Soviet monitoring in 1986 did not distinguish I-131 species → additional uncertainty in retrospective thyroid dose reconstruction
source: dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv; ICRP 30 1979; Chamberlain 1984; UNSCEAR 2008 dosimetry chapter

chernobyl_relevance: I-129 (t1/2=15.7×10⁶ yr) released from Chernobyl: ~0.18 TBq total (vs I-131 1760 PBq); essentially no radiological significance (low specific activity); but I-129/I-127 ratio used as ultra-sensitive tracer of nuclear fuel processing; detectable in Baltic and North Sea as tracer of reprocessing releases (UK Sellafield; La Hague France) which dominate over Chernobyl I-129 contribution
notes: I-129 stable isotope tracer for marine chemistry; Chernobyl contribution negligible vs fuel reprocessing I-129; mentioned here as context for iodine environmental chemistry completeness

chernobyl_relevance: 400,000 thyroid measurements performed in Belarus and Ukraine in first weeks post-accident; most using DP-100 instruments (poorly calibrated for I-131 neck geometry; ~3x uncertainty in dose); only ~200 measurements considered reliable retrospectively; medical professionals untrained for in vivo thyroid counting; measurements performed without systematic record-keeping
notes: The 400,000 measurement figure is cited in Soviet/Russian literature but quality is very poor; UNSCEAR notes most were not usable for dose reconstruction; only reliable data from special studies (Belarus 1986 by Malko and others); contributed to RADRUE method needing Monte Carlo to characterize measurement uncertainty

chernobyl_relevance: Populations in Belarus, Ukraine, Russia in 1986 had endemic iodine deficiency (dietary iodine intake <100 µg/day vs recommended 150 µg/day); iodine-deficient thyroid is more metabolically active, absorbs I-131 MORE avidly, and has lower stable iodine pool to dilute I-131; effectively amplifies thyroid dose by factor 1.5-3x vs iodine-sufficient population
notes: This explains why thyroid cancer incidence in Chernobyl-affected populations was higher than predicted by UNSCEAR models using standard thyroid uptake factors; and why the same I-131 doses in Western Europe (iodine-sufficient from ocean fish diet) caused fewer thyroid cancers
source: Cardis 2005 Eur J Cancer; UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D para D213; thyroid_cancer_timeseries_REAL.csv

chernobyl_relevance: Potassium iodide (KI) blocks I-131 uptake by saturating thyroid with stable I-127; mechanism: thyroid absorbs available iodine without discriminating I-127 vs I-131; pre-loading with stable KI means essentially zero I-131 uptake; >90% protection if given within 2 hours of exposure; 50% if given at same time; <10% if given 6+ hours after
notes: Dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv already documents KI effectiveness; Poland gave KI to 18M people; USSR gave KI to almost nobody; Soviet failure to distribute KI remains one of the most criticizable decisions of the Chernobyl response; cost of KI = pennies per dose; thyroid cancer prevention value = enormous

chernobyl_relevance: I-131 t1/2=8.02 days; by 3 months post-accident (July 1986): I-131 activity = 0.5^11.2 = 0.0004 of initial = 0.04% remaining; by October 1986 effectively zero; all subsequent thyroid cancer from Chernobyl is from dose received in first 8 weeks (April-June 1986); no new I-131 thyroid dose possible after July 1986
notes: This sharp decay is why I-131 is so dangerous in acute phase but irrelevant long-term; Cs-137 (t1/2=30yr) poses chronic low-dose ingestion risk for decades; the two isotopes represent completely different risk profiles in time
